sections.heading: Starting up a Subsidiary in India: Your Ultimate Guide to registering a Subsidiary Company in India
paragraphs: Do you intend to increase your business presence in India? Formation of a subsidiary is one of the most reliable and stable strategies. Here, we are going to take you through the whole procedure of registering an Indian subsidiary company, explain why it is usually the most appropriate company registration in Indian subsidiary enterprises and how a subsidiary business in India can open growth opportunities.
It is a good place to start before getting into the formalities, why so appealing an avenue is the Indian subsidiary registration:
Separate legal personality: When it is incorporated, the subsidiary becomes a discrete legal entity - liabilities, assets, agreements and liabilities belong to it (not to the parent).
Limited liability: Shareholder (including the parent) protection up to an extent of their investments.
100 percent FDI permitted: In most of the industries, any foreign firm can have 100 percent ownership in the Indian company where it is registered without any pre-registration permission.

Accessibility to local bank and credit facilities: There is a better opportunity of a local entity to open bank accounts, take loans and conduct business in Indian currency, which is not easy with foreign entities.
Perpetual succession: The subsidiary is not subject to alteration in its management or shareholding that will impact the continuation.
Tax and regulatory benefits: India has tax treaties, special economic zone incentives, local compliance, and so on.
Due to these benefits, the subsidiary registration in India has become the best entry and operating mode of many multinational groups in the Indian market.
You are free in making several structural decisions when you decide to proceed with subsidiary company registration in India. The most common ones include:
Wholly Owned Subsidiary
The parent company has 100 percent of the share capital. This provides total control of the operations, policies and decision making.
Partially Owned Subsidiary
The parent does not have the absolute control but only a substantial proportion (say >50% or less). The owners can be local partners or investors.
Joint Venture Subsidiary
